mode_parking_about: Street Space Editor maps and edits on-street parking and related street-space data in OpenStreetMap.
mode_parking_thanks_after: for the inspiration and initial code that started this mode.
mode_width_about: Inspect and edit highway width in OpenStreetMap. Select a road to view its width and adjust it with draggable side handles.
mode_bicycle_about: Inspect and edit bicycle infrastructure on OpenStreetMap ways. Classify cycleways, apply TILDA-style category suggestions, and edit bike-related tags.
mode_lanes_about: Three-column lane editor: select geometry on the map, read the plan sketch in the middle, and edit all lanes in the attribute matrix. Walk the street chain to keep neighbouring segments in view.
mode_table_about: Compare and edit all OSM tags across neighbouring highway segments in a spreadsheet-style matrix. Walk the street chain, propagate values from the center segment, and save through the shared changeset.
mode_surface_about: Inspect and edit highway surface and smoothness in OpenStreetMap. Select a way to view tagged coverage and apply surface/smoothness tags.
mode_sidewalks_about: Inspect and edit sidewalk mapping in OpenStreetMap. Coming soon.
mode_stub_panel: This mode is not available yet. Parking mode remains fully editable; edits stay in the shared changeset.

width_guide_road_kerb_body: Measure kerb to kerb (edge to edge of the carriageway) as width=*. Include on-street parking and on-carriageway cycle lanes. Exclude sidewalks, separate cycle tracks, and street_side parking. Shoulders (shoulder=*) are situational — count them only when they are part of the paved carriageway. This is kerb-to-kerb, not building-to-building. On unmarked roads (lane_markings=no), prefer surveying width=* (+ parking) over guessing lanes=* from metres alone.
width_guide_road_kerb_note: width:lanes is one pipe tag over flowing-traffic slots only (e.g. motor|bike). Parking and buffers are not pipes — use parking:*:width and cycleway:*:buffer. If a bike lane appears both in width:lanes and in cycleway:*:width, do not double-count — pick one modelling style per way.
width_guide_road_parking_branch_body: Parking on the carriageway (parking:*=lane) sits inside width=*. Parking bays in the roadside space (parking:*=street_side) sit outside the baseline kerb and must not be included. When the kerb steps in and out, fix one baseline carriageway width. Permanent edge parking is not a lanes=* / width:lanes slot — count moving motor lanes only. This width editor does not write parking tags — use the parking mode.
width_guide_road_width_lanes_body: width:lanes is a single pipe-separated list (left→right), e.g. width:lanes=3|2 for motor then bike. Write one tag — the pipes are the per-slot list. Each slot is the clear width between markings (paint excluded; logical assumption, not wiki text). Pipe slots follow the :lanes schema (bike yes, parking no) and are not the same as lanes=* (motor flowing lanes only). Buffers stay on cycleway:*:buffer. This editor does not write width:lanes today.
width_guide_road_width_vs_lanes_body: Carriageway width=* is usually larger than the sum of width:lanes pipes — the tags answer different questions (StreetComplete keeps asking for width even when width:lanes exists). A useful check: width ≈ Σ width:lanes + Σ paint (+ parking / shoulder / buffer / gutter). Parking width is never a width:lanes pipe. In Germany, longitudinal strokes are about 0.12 m (Schmalstrich) or 0.25 m (Breitstrich). Do not use width:effective — its measurement boundary is undefined; prefer width plus the parking scheme, or width:lanes. This editor does not write width:lanes today.
width_guide_cycleway_clear_body: For marked bike lanes, measure the clear riding width between the boundary lines as cycleway:*:width — do not include the paint strokes (Berlin / Verkehrswende practice). On a separate highway=cycleway, use plain width=*.
width_guide_cycleway_buffer_body: A painted or hatched separator from traffic is tagged as cycleway:*:buffer in metres. Buffer widths include the boundary lines and hatching (Berlin / ERA practice). By contrast, cycleway:*:width is only the clear riding strip between those boundaries. This editor does not write buffer tags today.
width_guide_path_segregated_body: On a shared path with segregated=yes, tag the overall surface as width=* and the parts as cycleway:width and footway:width. How marking thickness between foot and cycle relates to those keys is an open question — there is no established OSM rule. This editor does not write these split keys today.
width_guide_path_segregated_note: Do not invent a paint formula here; unlike carriageway width:lanes, there is no established marking rule for segregated paths.
width_guide_sidewalk_body: Tag a typical usable width along the sidewalk as sidewalk:*:width — not the absolute minimum at a local pinch point. Sidewalk width sits outside carriageway width=*. Edging stones (Randsteine) left and right of the paved strip are drawn as kerbs but are not part of sidewalk:*:width (or any other :width) — measure the clear walkable metres between them.
width_guide_verge_body: A real grass strip, berm, or tree lawn is tagged with verge=* and optionally verge:*:width. Those metres sit outside carriageway width=*. Tiny indentations into a sidewalk (tree pits, short nudges) are ignored when judging sidewalk width — they are not a verge. Sidewalk edging stones (Randsteine) left and right of the paved strip are drawn as kerbs but are not counted in any :width on this figure — sidewalk:left:width is only the clear walkable metres between them. This editor does not write verge tags today.
width_guide_other_path_body: Measure the usable surface width of this way as width=*. Where the width changes substantially, split the way and tag each segment. Rural / unpaved definitions can diverge from urban kerb rules — prefer measured width=* when you can.
width_guide_maxwidth_vs_width_body: width=* is the physical width of the feature (road surface, path, …). maxwidth=* is a legal vehicle limit, usually signed. maxwidth:physical=* is a physical clearance (gate, pier, …) with no sign required. Do not confuse these three. This editor writes width only.
width_guide_est_width_provenance_body: When you only guess the width, prefer est_width=* over inventing a precise width=*. Record how you got the figure with source:width=*. This app already sets source:width when you measure from aerial imagery. On unmarked roads, width=* (+ parking) is more verifiable than inventing lanes=* from metres alone.
width_guide_narrowings_body: Where the carriageway narrows for a stretch, split the way and tag the local width=* (or est_width) on that segment. Optionally add narrow=yes and/or hazard=road_narrows. Routers should use the minimum width along a segment, not an average.
width_guide_row_composition_body: There is no single OSM tag for the full street cross-section. Compose it from components: sidewalk:*:width + verge:*:width + carriageway width=* (plus separate areas for medians). Do not invent an aggregate key.
width_guide_illustrative_caption: Illustrative metres — not from a research scenario.
width_guide_edge_legend_clear: Clear-width ticks sit on the inner face of paint (markings outside the arrow).
width_guide_edge_legend_inclusive: Inclusive ticks (width=*, buffer) sit on kerb faces / outer paint faces; kerb body is drawn outside the carriageway.
width_guide_kerb_vs_paint: Stone block = kerb / sidewalk edging (Randstein) — barrier only, not part of any :width. Dark strip = road marking (paint).
width_guide_way_orientation: ↑ = OSM way direction. Diagram left = *:left, diagram right = *:right. cycleway:right:buffer:left is the left side of a right-hand cycleway (Separation proposal).
parking_datetime_title: If parking:condition present, show kind of parking at this time of day and day of week.
legend_width_rules_intro: Used when a way has no parseable width or est_width. The oneway column applies for one-way motor traffic: oneway=yes or -1, implicit on motorway/motorway_link and junction=roundabout, or oneway:bicycle=no on a one-way road. Unknown highway types use 10 m.
